route: 5 (subscale/block structure, via the inter-item correlation signature) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution) + 3-analogue (deposit total reproduces the raw unreversed sum; known sex difference fixes the direction)
evidence: Structural signature over all 468 respondents (verify_rosetti2023_gad7.R, live irw_fetch). P1 content outlier: mean inter-item r is 0.391 for GAD7_q6 against 0.427 (q7), 0.445 (q5), 0.528 (q2), 0.538 (q1), 0.546 (q3), 0.546 (q4) -- q6 is the lowest by 0.036, as canonical item 6 'Becoming easily annoyed or irritable' should be among six worry/tension items. P2 somatic pair: GAD7_q5's strongest correlate is GAD7_q4 at 0.580, next 0.516 (q3), 0.478 (q1), 0.450 (q2), 0.334 (q7), 0.313 (q6) -- the canonical 'trouble relaxing' / 'so restless it is hard to sit still' pair. P3 option axis: raw 0-3 sum is 9.64 for the 306 women vs 6.83 for the 155 men (flipped coding would read 11.36 vs 14.17, i.e. men more anxious), the sum rises monotonically with time on social media (6.13 <1hr, 7.80 1-2hr, 9.00 2-3hr, 8.99 3-4hr, 11.15 >4hr), correlates +0.363 with the deposit's CAS total, and the deposit's own GAD7_sum equals the raw unreversed sum exactly (max abs diff 0, range 0-21). Per-item means 1.462 (q3) > 1.449 (q4) > 1.427 (q6) > 1.329 (q1) > 1.109 (q7) > 1.030 (q5) > 0.929 (q2) are reproduced identically by the live IRW table and the figshare source, confirming the melt is by column name. NOT ESTABLISHED: this route pins GAD7_q5 and GAD7_q6 and the response direction only; GAD7_q1, GAD7_q2, GAD7_q3, GAD7_q4 and GAD7_q7 are NOT distinguished from one another -- a permutation among those five would survive every check above, and no per-item statistics are published anywhere accessible to break the tie (paper closed access, deposit unlabelled). Hence PARTIAL.

route: route 3 (published/deposited subscale totals) + route 1/8 (cross-sample per-item mean, SD and skew profile)
evidence: Route 3: the deposit's own summary columns are reproduced by the canonical blocks exactly, as integer identities over all 468 rows -- CEI_sum=sum(CAS_q1..q8) 468/468, FI_sum=sum(q9..q13) 468/468, EXP_sum=sum(q14..q16) 468/468, BEH_sum=sum(q17..q22) 468/468, CAS_sum=sum(q1..q13) 468/468; moving a boundary one item breaks it (CEI_sum=sum(q1..q7) 200/468, FI_sum=sum(q10..q14) 163/468). That pins every item's subscale membership and the 8/13/16/22 boundaries. Route 1/8: the 22 observed means (0-4) against Behavioral Sciences 2023;13(12):966 Table A1 re-indexed to canonical order give Spearman rho=0.912 against a 2000-draw permutation null whose 95th pct of |rho| is 0.423; largest agreements q7 0.40 vs 0.34, q14 1.44 vs 1.46, q19 3.66 vs 3.50, q20 2.86 vs 2.90. The q14/q15 near-tie (1.436 vs 1.410, gap 0.026) is broken by dispersion in the published direction: SD 1.24<1.35 (published 1.03<1.18) and skew 0.47<0.52 (published 0.31<0.76). NOT ESTABLISHED: order within a subscale. The cross-sample rho is driven by between-block level differences -- within-block it is only +0.69 (CEI, 8 items) and +0.54 (BEH, 6 items), so a swap of two similar items inside one subscale would survive this check. Hence PARTIAL.

ROUTE 1 (cross-sample per-item means; verify_rosetti_2023_gad7.R). Live per-item means over all 468 respondents, GAD7_q1..q7 = 1.329 / 0.929 / 1.462 / 1.449 / 1.030 / 1.427 / 1.109, against Martinez-Vazquez et al. (2022) PeerJ 10:e14296 Table 2 (n=170 SPANISH-LANGUAGE nursing students, items 1-7) = 1.38 / 0.82 / 1.38 / 1.18 / 0.83 / 1.12 / 0.91. Spearman under the identity mapping rho = 0.8469 (p = 0.016); the identity ranks 43rd of all 5040 relabellings of the seven live columns (top 0.85%, best relabelling r = 0.991). The three least-endorsed live items are exactly {q2, q5, q7} and so are the three least-endorsed published items, in the same order (q2 < q5 < q7 live, 0.82 < 0.83 < 0.91 published) -- including the non-obvious result that item 2 ('Not being able to stop or control worrying'), not item 5, is the floor item in both samples. OPTION AXIS: the deposit's GAD7_sum equals the raw unreversed sum of GAD7_q1..q7 exactly (max |diff| = 0.0, mean 8.74, SD 4.87, range 0-21; a flipped 0-3 coding would give 21 - 8.74 = 12.26), and corr(GAD7_sum, CAS_sum) = +0.363, the direction the paper reports, so the items are stored raw with 0 = 'Not at all'. DOES NOT ESTABLISH: q1, q3, q4 and q6 are not distinguished from one another -- their live means span only 1.329-1.462 and the comparator's own items 1 and 3 are tied at 1.38, so a permutation within that block of four would survive this route; the q2-vs-q5 ordering rests on a 0.10 gap in one sample. Hence PARTIAL.

route: 3 (published subscale totals: M and SD, paper Table 2) + partition-discrimination permutation test
evidence: Rosharudin et al. (2023) Table 2 publishes DASS-21 subscale M/SD for this same N=689 sample. Summing the seven items each code letter assigns: Stress 10.888/5.997 vs published 10.96/6.02; Anxiety 9.776/5.684 vs 9.84/5.68; Depression 9.782/6.330 vs 9.86/6.34 -- all three SDs within 0.023, all three means 0.064-0.078 BELOW published (a constant offset of unknown origin; the deposit holds exactly the 689 complete records the paper says it analysed). Combined |dM|+|dSD| score 0.084 for this partition against min 0.154 / median 0.790 over 2000 random 7/7/7 partitions of the same 21 items, i.e. 2000/2000 rival partitions are worse, so the S/A/D partition is discriminated. DOES NOT ESTABLISH the order of the seven items WITHIN each subscale: that rests on the canonical DASS-21 item numbering reproduced by the number in each code (@3_D = item 3), and no per-item statistic is published for this sample. Also establishes nothing about the option/resp axis, which ships blank (5 live levels 0-4 vs the instrument's 4 anchors). Hence PARTIAL.
